At /O2 /Ob2 /MD /G5 all three are relocation-masked exact and unique in gog-base, demo (+0x360), both 1.261 executables and the 1.28 base; absent from the packed Wiz8_v128.exe and protected retail, recorded as unavailable. /G6 mismatches Random and Chance; /Ob2 is required because Wizardry inlined Random into Chance and constant-folded the range to 100 - under plain /O2 the unit misleadingly looks like two exacts and one missing function. 0x0040EFA0's masked hash 438ef441... equals the repo's existing hand-port hash, so the original name is Random and CFAgent's GetRandomNumber becomes an alias. Two of three exact, plus one extra. GetMonsterDataByID 115/115 at 0x004E57C0 (5976911974dc...) first build. GetRandomCharacter 218/218 at 0x00518150 (f881acd9b355...) after one correction. PrintNothingHappenedOrSpecialItemRequired NOT attempted - it is a __thiscall method on an unrecovered class reading field 0x23C and dispatching through an unnamed 5-argument routine at 0x0058AC00; it needs a class boundary first, so it is better done alongside that class than guessed at here.

GetMonsterDataByID: the canonical assertion text is real original evidence - it names the parameter uiMonsterSpecies and the bound MAX_MONSTERS_IN_DATABASE (1000), and places the function at Local Code\\MonsterManager.cpp:1523. It caches 0x297-byte MONSTERS.DBS runtime records, which matches the already-tracked record size, and loads through the already-named LoadMonsterDatabaseRecord (0x0054A8A0).

GetRandomCharacter: came out at exactly 218 bytes on the first build with only 5 mnemonic mismatches, all from two source-level facts - W8Character 0x0b01 and 0x0b11 are UNSIGNED (canonical compares are JB/JBE, signed ints give JL/JE), and 'scanned' must be initialized before 'slot' to reproduce the xor order. Also matches in the demo at 0x0051C230. Widened W8Character with faction at 0x75 and the two gating fields; verified CharacterPointerToPartySlot and GetProfessionCasterLevel still match exactly after the restructure.

Pattern worth carrying forward: for the second port running, the residual difference was signedness and declaration order, not anything structural. Combined with wiz8-4of.1's finding that register roles followed control-flow shape, the 7 structurally-strong entries may be closer than their notes suggest.
